prompt_context_by_prefix.consent:
Use these preferred technical term translations when relevant:
- count (tally): [needs translation sprint]
    DO NOT render as: the sense of MATTERING or being valued — "your visit counts", "make it count". This is a live English idiom and the most likely wrong reading; it turns a request for permission into a compliment; the sense of RELYING on somebody — "count on me"; the accounting or financial sense — an account, a balance, a reckoning of money; the noble title — count, as in a European rank. A real trap in Romance and Slavic languages, where the tallying verb and the title can share a root; rendering it as MEASURE or TRACK, both of which imply more than we do. We add one to a total; we do not measure or follow anybody
- cookie (browser storage): [needs translation sprint]
    DO NOT render as: the food — a biscuit, a sweet baked good. This is the literal meaning of the English word and the failure mode to expect, especially where the computing sense has not been borrowed; coining a descriptive phrase where your language already borrows 'cookie'. A visitor hunting for cookie settings will not recognise an invented term; widening it to all browser storage. The privacy notice distinguishes cookies from localStorage and IndexedDB deliberately, because they are listed as separate rows
- log (record): [needs translation sprint]
    DO NOT render as: the timber sense — a felled tree, a log of wood. This is the literal meaning of the English word and the failure mode to expect; the mathematical sense — logarithm. 'Log' abbreviates both in English, and in a suite full of engineering formulas this is a live confusion; the sense of LOGGING IN or signing in to an account. There are no accounts on this site at all, so any rendering that suggests one is wrong twice over; rendering it as MONITOR, TRACK or FOLLOW, all of which imply watching a person over time. We write one line saying a page was opened; we do not follow anybody; borrowing the English word where an ordinary verb for recording exists
prompt_context_by_prefix.lpn:
Use these preferred technical term translations when relevant:
- flow (Q): debi
- velocity (v): hız
- head (H): yük
    DO NOT render as: a lazy anatomical calque that is NOT the language's natural hydraulic term — but an anatomically-derived word that IS the dominant local standard is correct (English 'head' is itself the body-part word repurposed); defer to the cultural standard, do not 'fix' a natural term for containing a body-part morpheme; pressure (head is a length/energy-per-weight, not a pressure); source/origin of a stream
- head loss (h_L): yük kaybı
    DO NOT render as: pressure loss / pressure drop (use the head-loss term, not the pressure term); a lazy anatomical calque that is not the local standard — an anatomically-derived word that IS the dominant standard is correct; see 'head' root entry
- friction loss (h_f): sürtünme kaybı
- minor loss (h_m): yerel kayıp
- pressure (p): Basınç
    DO NOT render as: the HEAD term (a height of water column) — pressure here is what a gauge reads; atmospheric or meteorological pressure senses; a stress or material-strength sense; figurative 'pressure' (urgency, coercion)
- elevation (z): Kot
    DO NOT render as: the HEAD term — an elevation is a position above a datum, not an energy; a generic 'tall/high' adjective where the language has a surveying term; altitude in the aviation or geographic sense where a levelled survey term exists
- demand: Talep
    DO NOT render as: economic or market demand; a legal demand/claim; a request in the everyday sense
- static head (H): Statik besleme yükü
    DO NOT render as: electrostatic / static electricity; 'stationary/motionless' in a non-hydraulic sense
- maximum allowable head (H): İzin ver. maks. boru basıncı
    DO NOT render as: the operating / computed head (this is a fixed design limit, not the pressure the network actually develops)
- supply head (H): Besleme yükü
    DO NOT render as: an economic 'supply'; confusing supply (source) head with the delivered/residual head at a demand point
- supply curve: besleme eğrisi
    DO NOT render as: an economic supply curve; a demand curve
- looped network: halkalı boru şebekesi
    DO NOT render as: a control-flow / programming loop; a physical loop, knot, or coil
- branched network: Dallı Boru Şebekesi
    DO NOT render as: a literal botanical 'tree' where the language has a proper network/graph term; a looped or meshed network (branched means no loops)
- pipe line: Boru hatları
    DO NOT render as: a queue or line of people; a rope, cord, or cable; a line of text; a purely geometric line/segment
- pressure rating: İzin ver. maks. boru basıncı
    DO NOT render as: a stress or material strength rather than a water pressure; blood-pressure or tyre-pressure senses; a general word for strong or high
- pressure reduction: basınç düşürme
    DO NOT render as: naming a specific device (break pressure tank, BPT, pressure-reducing valve) as if the tool recommends one; depressurizing in the sense of emptying or draining the pipe
- energy grade line (EGL): enerji çizgisi
- Manning roughness (n): Manning pürüzlülük katsayısı
- friction factor (f): sürtünme faktörü
- draw (a diagram): çizmek
    DO NOT render as: draw water (abstract, pump, or take water from a source) -- the wrong sense here, and PLAUSIBLE in a hydraulics context, which is what makes it dangerous; pull, drag, or haul; draw as in a lottery or a tie/stalemate; withdraw money
- junction: düğüm
    DO NOT render as: a road junction, crossroads, or intersection; a physical pipe fitting (tee, cross, elbow) -- a junction here is a point in the model, not a part you buy; a railway junction; an electrical junction box
- reservoir: rezervuar
    DO NOT render as: a tank whose level changes over time -- lpn_ explicitly does NOT model tanks (see lpn_notes_2_def), and calling this one would promise time-varying behaviour that does not exist; a natural lake specifically, where the language has a general storage/supply term; a reserve or reservation in the non-physical sense
- node: düğüm
    DO NOT render as: a computing/server node (a transliterated loanword where the language has a real graph or network-diagram term); a knot, lump, or swelling (the anatomical/botanical sense of the Latin root); a node in the wave-physics sense (a point of zero amplitude)
- link: hat
    DO NOT render as: a hyperlink or web link -- the dominant modern sense of the English word, and the wrong one here; a chain link (the physical object); a connection in the social or logistical sense
- vertex: kırılma noktası
    DO NOT render as: a mathematical vertex of a polygon or a parabola apex, where the language has a plainer word for a bend or corner point in a drawn line; a peak or summit; a vertex in the anatomical sense (crown of the head)
- background image: arka plan görüntüsü
    DO NOT render as: a backdrop in the theatrical/stage sense (the English source word was CHANGED to "background image" in Task 193 precisely to remove this transliteration lure); a wallpaper or decorative background; an online/satellite map layer -- this is a plain image file the user already has
- pump curve: pompa eğrisi
    DO NOT render as: a curve in the geometric/road sense; a pump characteristic confused with an efficiency or power curve -- this one is head against flow
- project (saved network): proje
    DO NOT render as: an engineering project or job in the contractual sense (a scheme, a works, a contract) -- this is a saved document; a projection (optical or cartographic); to project or forecast
- scenario: senaryo
    DO NOT render as: a scene or setting in the dramatic/film sense; a scenario in the "worst case story" narrative sense, where the language has a modelling or variant-case term; a copy or duplicate of the network -- a scenario is a set of differences, not a second network
- zoom to extents: Tümünü göster
    DO NOT render as: a general "adjust/change the zoom" — this is the trap. es "Ajustar zoom" and pt "Zoom para ajustar" both shipped meaning ADJUST THE ZOOM, which describes the zoom slider, not this button. A verb meaning adjust/regulate/set is wrong unless the label also says WHAT is fitted; zoom in / zoom out / a zoom level or percentage — this command has no direction and no amount; a transliterated "zoom" loanword standing alone, where the language has a real word for showing the whole drawing; the photographic or camera sense of zoom (a lens movement)
- default (setting): varsayılan
    DO NOT render as: the financial sense — failure to pay a debt, defaulting on a loan. This is the dominant everyday sense of the English word in many languages and the single most dangerous confusion here; the legal sense — failure to appear or to act, a default judgment; a bare "reset" or "restore" with the default concept dropped entirely. ro shipped calc_defaults as just "Reseteaza" (Reset) while its own calc_defaults_confirm used "valorile implicite" correctly — the button must say WHAT is restored; a word meaning normal/usual/ordinary where the language has a real settings term. sw shipped "maadili ya kawaida" (normal values) instead of "chaguo-msingi"; "kawaida" describes what is typical, not what the software ships with; the sports sense — winning or losing by default, by forfeit
- upstream: memba
- downstream: mansap

consent.context: To add something to a running total. Used throughout the Task 286 consent banner (consent_body, consent_current_granted, consent_current_denied) and the privacy notice, where the whole ask is whether a visitor may be counted once rather than once per visit. The distinction the word carries here is VISITORS vs VISITS: a visitor is a person tallied once; a visit is a single page load. Use whatever ordinary verb your language uses for tallying or totalling; there is nothing technical about it, and the risk is entirely in the wrong sense being chosen.

consent.context: To write down that something happened, in a file kept on the server. What EngCalcs logs is that a page was opened or a calculation was run — the page name, the language, and the time — with no IP address, no account and no identifier of any kind. Used throughout the Task 286 consent banner and privacy notice. The everyday verb your language uses for RECORDING an event is the right choice; there is nothing technical about it, and no language needs to borrow the English word.

lpn.context: Hydraulic head — energy per unit weight of water, expressed as a height of water column. The ROOT concept behind head loss, velocity head, weir head, and gross/net head. A length, never a pressure. Appears as a bare label in Weir Flow (ws_headWaterHeight), Orifice (or_head), and Manning Pipe Flow (mpf_velocity_head). Acceptable English synonyms (translate the concept, not the exact word): energy elevation, hydraulic grade line (HGL).
lpn.translation_notes: Newly seeded 2026-07-20 to close the long-standing gap where only the COMPOUNDS (head loss, velocity/weir/gross/net head) had entries but the root word 'head' did not — the root is what every agent re-derived (and sometimes mistranslated as anatomical head or pressure). Values below are the roots extracted from those compound entries and are best-effort/derived, not natively verified — confirm in the term-centric sweep (see ROADMAP). Several languages split the root by sense: the hydro-power 'fall' sense uses a different word than the pipe 'head' sense (cs spád vs tlaková výška; hr/sr visina·pad vs visina; ro sarcină vs cădere; tr yük vs düşü; ar علو/الارتفاع vs الضغط). Where that split exists, keep the pipe/energy-head root here and let the fall-sense compounds keep their own word. Slavic напор/напір, sw kimo (corrected from kichwa — see 2026-07-22 note below), and the هد/ہیډ/ہیڈ/हेड/ሄድ loanword family are consistent and documented across the suite (see 'head loss' notes). [2026-07-21 Task 128 RESOLVED — Tom decision] Native review is not realistically available for these; rely on AI guidance and defer to the locally natural term. Anatomically-derived head words are NOT inherently wrong (English 'head' is itself anatomical) — a blanket anatomical-head avoid was mistaken and has been reframed above. Accordingly: my or_head/ws_headWaterHeight 'ခေါင်းဆုံး' (contains ခေါင်း) is KEPT as a locally natural term — NOT a defect; the earlier ဖိမြင့်ဆင့် root is one acceptable variant, ခေါင်းဆုံး is another, both stand. he or_head/ws_headWaterHeight 'עומק' (depth) is KEPT as-is — for orifice effective head a depth-to-centroid reading is physically legitimate, and it is a natural term. This does NOT license reverting the documented cs/he/sw velocity-head calque fixes (rychlostní výška, עומד מהירות, kimo cha kasi): those were replaced because the anatomical word was not the natural term there, which the reframed avoid guard still forbids. hi: or_head uses शीर्ष, velocity-head same शीर्ष, root here is the हेड loanword — harmless internal variance, polish only. [2026-07-21 Task 131 tip sprint] Definitional tips now ship in all 26 languages on or_head/ws_headWaterHeight/mpf_velocity_head ('energy per unit weight of water, a height of water column, not a pressure' / 'kinetic energy as a height of water column'), anchoring the concept at point-of-use. am head re-verified CLEAN this pass: uses the ሄድ loanword, no ጭንቅ (distress) calque anywhere. my (ခေါင်းဆုံး) and he (עומק) or_head/ws labels CLOSED 2026-07-21 as locally natural (see Task 128 resolution above) — no label change made. Task 130 (2026-07-21): am odt_ keys (odt_h1, odt_notes_1_def) still carried the ጭንቅ (distress) calque for head, missed by earlier sweeps; fixed to ሄድ. [2026-07-22 sw head family → kimo, Tom + Kenya-engineer input] REVERSES 'sw kichwa': kichwa (body-part head) is NOT the Swahili engineering term for hydraulic head. Anchor — velocity head was already 'kimo cha kasi' (the accepted descriptive term), so kimo is the register's word for head and kichwa was a body-part calque. Applied across the sw lang file (mhp_gross_head, mhp_hl_check, mhp_notes_3_def, rc_notes_7_def, odt_notes_1_def, or_head + ws_headWaterHeight labels): head=kimo cha maji, head loss=upotevu wa kimo, gross=kimo cha jumla cha maji, net=kimo halisi cha maji, weir head=kimo cha maji juu ya kizingiti. Ride-alongs same pass: crown taji(royal)→kilele (or_ orifice crown; rc_ crest already kilele); weir kizuizi/bwawa→kizingiti cha maji ('water sill', incl. ws_/wi_ calculator identities, Lenye→Chenye noun-class agreement); specific gravity uzito maalum KEPT. RATIONALE: for the 0.65 low-resource languages engineering discourse happens in English (TZ/KE engineering education is English-medium); the local tongue lives at the field/extension register, so there is no fixed engineering-Swahili standard to defer to — descriptive clarity for a Swahili-speaking field worker is the goal, and TANZANIA is the specific target audience (Tom's Kenya engineer). See memory project_low_resource_register_reality. [2026-07-27 sw kichwa->kimo COMPLETED, ROADMAP Task 147] The 2026-07-22 decision above was only applied to the seven keys it named, leaving lib/lang.ec.sw.php split almost in half: 15 keys on kimo, 16 still on kichwa -- including the identity strings (menu + <title> + desc) of ALL THREE head-loss calculators (dw_, hw_, mphl_), which is the first thing a Swahili speaker saw. lpn.context: Energy loss expressed as a height of water column. Appears in Darcy-Weisbach, Hazen-Williams, Manning pipe, and Penstock calculators. Distinct from 'pressure drop' — use the hydraulic engineering term.
lpn.translation_notes: 'Head' in the hydraulic sense (energy per unit weight) does not translate literally in many languages — use the established civil/hydraulic engineering phrase. The current 'губитак напора / gubitak tlačne visine' (= loss of hydraulic head) is more precise in a hydraulic engineering context and is preferred. lpn.context: A map/drawing toolbar command that rescales and recentres the view so the WHOLE drawing is visible at once — it computes the bounding box of every element and fits it to the window. The word "fit" in the English label is the lure — it invites a fitting/adjusting verb while saying nothing about what is fitted, so a translator with no other context reasonably lands on "adjust". THE ENGLISH IS DELIBERATELY UNCHANGED: "Zoom to fit" is an established UI idiom (browsers, PDF viewers, design tools all ship it) and renaming a recognized control costs more than guarding it — this entry plus its avoid array is the guard. Tom chose the PLAIN register for es and pt on 2026-08-08, so 3 of 4 now share the show-everything mental model while fr keeps its correct CAD form. Either register is acceptable for a new language; an adjust-the-zoom reading is not.

privacy.context: A small piece of information a website stores in a visitor's browser. NOTE THE LABEL'S JOB: it must be the phrase a visitor or a regulator LOOKS FOR, so the conventional term in your language beats a more descriptive one. Most languages simply keep the English word 'cookie', and where that is the convention it is the right answer.
privacy.translation_notes: Created 2026-08-12 alongside 'count (tally)', from the same Wave 0 pass. Empty translations for the same reason, with one extra: this is the term where deferring to the culture matters most, because the label's whole value is being the findable, conventional one. See CLAUDE.md, 'defer to cultural standard' — we are not the judges of terminology.

privacy.context: To write down that something happened, in a file kept on the server. What EngCalcs logs is that a page was opened or a calculation was run — the page name, the language, and the time — with no IP address, no account and no identifier of any kind. Used throughout the Task 286 consent banner and privacy notice. The everyday verb your language uses for RECORDING an event is the right choice; there is nothing technical about it, and no language needs to borrow the English word.
privacy.translation_notes:
Created 2026-08-12 at Tom's suggestion: *"There must be a better way to help translate 'logging' (recording) than to repeat that synonym in several _syn keys. Isn't that what our glossary is for?"* Exactly right, and this entry is the answer — the CONCEPT gloss belongs here once, not repeated in four labels. Note the boundary, which is easy to get wrong in the other direction: this replaces the repeated '(recording)' gloss, and NOT a label's own alternate wordings. See CLAUDE.md's routing rule and the retirement of the Task 132 trimming exception — the left-of-pipe is the payload, and a glossary pointer accompanies the synonyms rather than deleting them.

Translations empty on purpose, as with 'count (tally)' and 'cookie (browser storage)': every language has a settled ordinary verb for this, we have nothing attested, and inventing 26 would be judging other people's terminology. The sprint fills them via the mandatory write-back.

rc.context: Volumetric flow rate. Appears in every calculator. Use the hydraulic/civil engineering term for discharge volume per unit time, not a general word for 'water flowing'.
rc.translation_notes: Spanish has two common terms: 'caudal' (Spain, South America) and 'gasto' (Mexico). Lead with 'caudal'. Portuguese: 'vazão' (Brazil) or 'caudal' (Portugal) — lead with 'vazão'. Pre-2026 sr/hr human translations used 'protok/protoka' — consistent with current glossary entries (confirmed match). bg RESOLVED (Tom, 2026-07-13): native engineer's 2026-07-06 clarification confirmed both 'дебит' (colloquial/general register) and 'водно количество' (academic/hydraulic-engineering register, used at university for Q) are acceptable. Tom decided suite-wide standardization on 'водно количество' — "I would put водно количество everywhere" — applied across all bg calculator categories (pipes/irrigation included, not just the hydraulic-structure/open-channel strings the engineer originally corrected). 'дебит' fully replaced in lib/lang.ec.bg.php 2026-07-13. Task 109 stages 3-5 (2026-07-19): bg standardized on водно количество (дебит drift removed from or_/mpf_/cs_ per Bulgarian-engineer-feedback.md); sr standardized on проток (stage 4); it confirmed on portata (flusso drift removed).

rc.context: Flow velocity (speed of water). Appears in all calculators.
rc.translation_notes: Most languages use a direct cognate of 'velocity'. Do not use a word meaning 'speed' in a general sense if a more precise hydraulic term exists. Pre-2026 sr/hr human translations used 'tečenja' (= flowing, a verbal noun from 'teći' = to flow) — this is less precise than the current 'brzina/брзина' (= speed/velocity) and the current AI-generated term is preferred.

rc.context: Angular rock placed to resist erosion on channel beds and banks. Appears in Manning Trapezoidal Channel and Rock Chute calculators.
rc.translation_notes: No direct single-word equivalent in most languages. Use the established local engineering term — this varies significantly by country. In Spanish, 'enrocado' (general) or 'escollera' (bank protection) are both used; lead with 'enrocado'. Bulgarian terms verified/corrected by a native Bulgarian engineer, 2026-07 (dev/Bulgarian-engineer-feedback.md). bg: 'каменна облицовка' (stone lining), not 'каменна наброска'. 2026-07-13 reconciliation pass (roadmap item 42): glossary updated to match incumbent, internally-consistent lang-file usage discovered by 5 independent category-5-wave-1 translation agents (it, pt, ru, tr) — glossary values were stale, not the shipped files. Task 97 (2026-07-13): tr's rock-chute (rc_) translation agent had actually diverged from this glossary value, using 'parça taşı' (rock fragment/piece) in 4 places instead of 'taş dolgu'; no native Turkish reviewer was available, so resolved by an AI (Opus) judgment call reasoning from suite convention — 'taş dolgu' ('stone fill', the established DSİ/TS term, cf. 'taş dolgu baraj' = rockfill dam) is correct for both the bulk-material and D50 particle-sizing senses, matching how es/fr/pt/ru all keep one bulk-material word rather than switching to a fragment/particle term for sizing contexts. Lang file corrected to 'taş dolgu' throughout; treat as our best-effort resolution, not pending native review (see CLAUDE.md 'Native review is real only when feedback actually lands'). Task 98 riprap audit (2026-07-13): found 6 of 26 languages (am, bn, he, hi, id, ur) had phonetically TRANSLITERATED the English word 'riprap' as a borrowed loanword instead of translating the concept — a real translation-quality defect, not a stylistic choice, concentrated in this specific bare/short-label term. English source renamed 'riprap' → 'rock lining' (see CLAUDE.md 'Write English source strings in Simple English') specifically because a transparent two-word English compound is much less likely to be transliterated than an opaque-looking jargon word; all 6 languages' rc_/mtc_ occurrences were corrected to real native terms in the same pass (each reusing that language's own already-successful translation pattern found elsewhere in its file). zh was separately found to use three inconsistent terms (块石/护坡/抛石) for this concept across different rc_ keys — not a transliteration issue, but the same 'pick one term and use it everywhere' defect — resolved by standardizing on 护坡 (slope protection/lining), which best matches the 'lining' sense and was already the plurality incumbent. The other 19 languages already had good native terms and needed no change — the concept translated fine, only the English word choice invited transliteration risk in weaker-resourced languages. Task 109 stage 2 (2026-07-19): ar/km/my/sw confirmed on real translated words — the phonetic-transliteration failure class (same as the 2026-07-13 rc_ audit) was checked and corrected where present.

rc.context: Dimensionless ratio of vertical drop to horizontal distance (rise/run). Used as channel slope (S_0) and friction slope in Manning and Darcy-Weisbach calculators. English aliases 'slope' and 'grade' (u_grade/u_gradePercent) both point here.
rc.translation_notes: WMO No. 385 entry 477 ('energy gradient') confirms Russian: 'энергетический уклон' (energy slope) — the base term 'уклон' is WMO-verified. In open-channel hydraulics, 'slope' is the energy gradient — not a geometric angle. Use the civil engineering term for gradient/grade, not a geographic or topographic term. [2026-07-21] Centralized the grade activity-sense guard here (was living only as u_grade/u_gradePercent label commentary): the 'avoid' array now carries the running/walking/jogging exercise-incline trap, so the slope entry is the single home for the grade→energy-gradient concept and its wrong senses.

rc.context: A steep rock-lined drop structure (also called a 'rock ramp') that conveys water rapidly down a slope in irrigation, drainage, or watershed management. Key concepts for translation: rock-lined, steep gradient, spillway or drop structure — translate the concept, not the English word 'chute'. The rock riprap matrix dissipates energy and resists erosion. Appears in Rock Chute Design (Robinson) and Robinson Rock Chute calculators.
rc.translation_notes: CRITICAL: 'Robinson' is the surname of K.M. Robinson, co-author of Robinson, Rice & Kadavy (1998) — it is a proper noun and must NEVER be translated or modified in any language. Translate only 'Rock Chute'. Concept to translate: 'rock-lined steep channel' or 'rock-lined spillway' — the drop/descent nature must be conveyed; a generic 'rock channel' is insufficient. CRITICAL for French: WMO No. 385 entry 517 establishes that the French word 'chute' means 'fall' (elevation difference) — it cannot name this structure. Use 'coursier en enrochement' (coursier = steep channel structure; enrochement = riprap). Spanish: USDA uses 'bajante de rocado' — 'bajante' (from bajar = to descend) correctly conveys the drop-structure nature; 'de rocado' = rock-lined. Russian: 'каменный быстроток' ('быстроток' = fast-flow/steep channel). Portuguese: changed from 'calha' (generic trough) to 'rampa em enrocamento' (rampa = ramp/slope, enrocamento = riprap) to convey steep character. Serbian: changed from 'жлеб' (gutter/trough) to 'брзоток' (fast-flow structure), consistent with ru/uk pattern. Bengali: changed from borrowed 'চ্যুট' (conveys nothing) to 'পাথর-আবৃত খাড়া নালা' (rock-lined steep channel). Persian: changed from generic 'آبراه سنگی' (stone waterway) to 'آبراه تند سنگچین' (تند = steep/swift, سنگچین = stone-laid/riprap). Pashto: added 'تند' (steep/swift) to original. Khmer: changed 'ចំហ' (open) to 'ជម្រាល' (sloped/inclined). NEEDS HUMAN REVIEW: am (ምቀጫ meaning uncertain), my (ထောင် may not clearly convey steep to all readers), de (Steinschütte is standard engineering term but doesn't explicitly say 'steep channel'). Turkish: changed to 'taş düşü' — 'düşü' is the established Turkish hydraulics term for a drop/chute structure (2026-07 audit; previous 'taş eğimli kanal' was descriptive but nonstandard). Spanish: NEEDS HUMAN VERIFICATION — 'bajante de rocado' claims a USDA source but 'rocado' is not standard Spanish ('enrocado' is); verify the USDA document or switch to 'bajante de enrocado'. 2026-07 reconciliation: fr/ro/ru/uk lang files updated to match this entry. NOT reconciled pending human review of the GLOSSARY side: hr 'kameni skluz' (consider 'kameni brzotok', parallel to sr/ru), bg 'каменна бързина' (consider 'каменен бързоток'), de 'Steinschütte' vs shipped 'Steingerinne' (both defensible - pick one). RESOLVED bg: native Bulgarian engineer confirmed 'каменен бързоток' (2026-07); lang file updated. Task 98 (2026-07-13): English source renamed 'Rock Chute' → 'Steep Channel' throughout the rc_ prefix (see CLAUDE.md 'Write English source strings in Simple English') — 'chute' itself is jargon-shaped English that some languages transliterated rather than translated. The earlier Bengali fix noted above only reached the calculator's title-level strings (rc_main_menu/rc_main_desc); a full-file grep found 'চ্যুট' still transliterated in 7 more rc_ body keys (rc_S0, rc_qt, rc_n_chute, rc_pond_ok_tip, rc_pond_warn_tip, rc_notes_2_def, rc_notes_3_def, rc_notes_7_def) — fixed 2026-07-13 to match the title's 'খাড়া নালা'. Hindi and Urdu had the same bare-transliteration defect suite-wide ('चूट'/'چوٹ') despite their titles being fine in some cases — fixed to 'तीव्र ढाल चैनल' (hi) and 'کھڑی نالی' (ur), applied consistently across every rc_ occurrence. Lesson: a healthy title-level translation does not guarantee the same concept was translated (vs. transliterated) in every short body label — check the whole file, not just the title strings, when auditing a jargon term.

rc.context: A steep open channel or drop structure for conveying water rapidly down a slope. Distinct from a gentle-slope irrigation canal. Per ec_lang_intent guidance: translate as 'steep channel' or 'spillway' — not as the word 'chute' borrowed into another language. Appears in Rock Chute Design (Robinson), Manning Trapezoidal Channel, and related drop-structure calculators.
rc.translation_notes: CRITICAL for French: WMO No. 385 entry 517 defines the English word 'fall' (elevation difference) as French 'chute', Spanish 'caída', and Russian 'падение'. The same pattern holds in all three WMO languages: the word for 'fall' (elevation difference) is NOT available for this hydraulic structure. 'Coursier' is the correct French term for the structure. Spanish: 'canal rápido'. Russian: 'быстроток' (the steep channel structure — distinct from 'падение' which means elevation fall). Chinese: '陡槽'. | [2026-07-20] Stage-6 sr audit found the glossary's own value (брзотек) was the stem-drift error; corrected to брзоток, consistent with ru/uk pattern and rc_ identity strings. | [2026-07-20] Stage-6 ps audit aligned to the file's own established identity-string term (تند اوبو لار) over a divergent glossary spelling, for cross-key consistency within category 5.

rc.context: Flow rate per unit width of channel (Q/B), in m²/s or ft²/s. The primary design input for the Robinson rock chute method. Appears in Rock Chute Design calculator.
rc.translation_notes: Use the hydraulic engineering term. 'Unit' here means 'per unit channel width' — not related to measurement units. Spanish: 'caudal unitario'. French: 'débit unitaire'. German: 'spezifischer Abfluss'. Russian: 'удельный расход'. Chinese: '单宽流量'. Bulgarian terms verified/corrected by a native Bulgarian engineer, 2026-07 (dev/Bulgarian-engineer-feedback.md). bg hydraulics uses 'водно количество' for discharge, not 'дебит'.

rc.context: The particle size at which 50% of the rock is finer by weight. The primary output of the Robinson rock chute method. Also used in Manning Trapezoidal Channel riprap sizing. The symbol D50 is universal — translate only the descriptive label.
rc.translation_notes: D50 (or D₅₀) is a universal engineering symbol — do not translate it. Translate only the label 'median rock size' or 'median particle size'. Most languages express this as 'median diameter'. Do not use 'average' (average ≠ median statistically). Spanish: 'tamaño mediano de roca'. French: 'taille médiane des rochers'. Chinese: '中值粒径'. **2026-07-13 cross-language research pass (item 44):** researched whether 'average/mean'-register wording (found in several languages' initial translations) is a real engineering error or defensible practice-register, using web research into each language's actual geotechnical/sedimentology literature. Confirmed real errors, corrected in both the lang files and this glossary: de ('mittlere'→'mediane'/'medianer', citing German BAW government sedimentology usage), cs ('střední'→'mediánová', citing Charles University hydraulics course), ru ('средний'→'медианный' for mi_d50in; rc_D50 already correct), tr ('orta'→'ortanca', matching the term already correct in rc_D50/rc_notes_1_def), fa ('متوسط'→'میانه', citing Persian percentile-based technical definitions), ur ('اوسط'/'درمیانی'/'درمیانہ'→'وسیط', mirroring Arabic's وسيط/متوسط distinction), sr ('средња'→'медијанска', matching mi_d50in which already used 'Медијана'). Found already correct in the lang files (glossary was simply stale, not the file — see item 42): bg ('медианен размер', confirmed live in mi_d50in/rc_D50/rc_notes_1_def), uk ('медіанний розмір'), hr ('medijalna veličina', an adjective form of medijan/medijana), ro ('dimensiunea mediană'). One language, am (Amharic), was researched and found to have no distinct circulating median-vs-average term at all — even Amharic dictionaries gloss 'median' as 'መካከለኛ' (same word used for 'middle/average') — so 'የድንጋይ መካከለኛ መጠን' was left unchanged; there's no more-correct term available in practice.

rc.context: The spread or uniformity of rock particle sizes. In the Robinson method, gradation is expressed as SD = D84.1/D50. Uniform rock ≈ 1.25; Robinson valid range 1.15–1.47. Appears in Rock Chute Design calculator.
rc.translation_notes: Use the geotechnical/hydraulic engineering term for grain size distribution or grading. Do not translate as 'grade' (implies quality). The symbol 'SD' and ratio notation D84.1/D50 are universal. Spanish/Portuguese: 'granulometría'/'granulometria'. French: 'granulométrie'. Russian/Bulgarian/Serbian: 'гранулометрический состав'. Chinese: '级配'. bg: native engineer confirmed 2026-07-06 the standard term for the D84.1/D50 gradation SD label is 'Коефициент на градация' (superseding the earlier 'коефициент на едрозърнестост' proposal and the alternative 'коефициент на разнозърненост'); applied in rc_SD/rc_SD_check. 2026-07-13 reconciliation pass (roadmap item 42): glossary updated to match incumbent, internally-consistent lang-file usage discovered by 5 independent category-5-wave-1 translation agents (it, pt, ru, tr) — glossary values were stale, not the shipped files.

rc.context: The fraction of the rock layer volume that is void space (air + water). Default 0.45 for angular crushed rock. Determines how much flow passes through the rock mantle versus over the surface. Appears in Rock Chute Design calculator. Distinct from Manning's n (roughness coefficient) — do not confuse the two.
rc.translation_notes: Standard hydraulic/geotechnical term with cognates in most European languages. Always distinguish from Manning 'n' in context — they appear in the same calculator.

rc.context: Dimensionless ratio of a material's density to the density of water (≈2.65 for crushed granite/basalt; Robinson valid range 2.54–2.82). Appears in Rock Chute Design and Manning Trapezoidal Channel. The English source keeps "specific gravity" — the standard English term and the one Robinson's paper uses (rc_ cites it). We deliberately do NOT swap it for "relative density" even though that reads as more modern: per Tom's principle (2026-07-20) we defer to each language's own dominant standard term rather than judging terminology.
rc.translation_notes: [2026-07-20 RESOLUTION — Tom's principle: 'we are not the judges of terminology, culture is.'] Use each language's dominant, culturally-standard term for this dimensionless concept, whatever its literal composition. A weight-flavored STANDARD term is CORRECT, not an error to be reformed toward 'relative density': tr 'özgül ağırlık', he 'משקל סגולי' (standard Hebrew physics-curriculum term), sr 'специфична тежина', ps 'ځانګړی ثقل' are the established local standards and stay. The ONLY hard rule is physical — the value is a dimensionless ratio and never carries units. hr RESOLVED to 'relativna gustoća', the dominant modern Croatian standard (gustoća = density), matching the shipped file; the glossary was the stale side. sw 'uzito maalum' is NOT an auto-defect: if it is the standard Swahili term for the concept used dimensionlessly (parallel to Turkish özgül ağırlık), it is correct — confirm it is the Swahili standard, do not replace it with a coined 'relative density' calque. This supersedes the earlier 'weight-word exception' framing, which wrongly implied 'relative density' was the target to push. [2026-07-21 assessment] Two more glossary values were stale vs. their shipped, internally-consistent files (same class as hr): sr updated 'специфична тежина'→'релативна густина' and it 'peso specifico relativo'→'densità relativa' to match each file's actual standard usage; no lang-file change needed. (Historical: de 'spezifisches Gewicht'→'relative Dichte' and ru 'удельный вес'→'относительная плотность' were corrected in the 2026-07-08 category-1 QA — those were genuine non-standard-in-context values, not the same as a language whose actual standard is weight-flavored.) [2026-07-21 Task 131 tip sprint] 'Density relative to water' definitional tip now ships in all 26 languages on mtc_sgrock/rc_sg. NEW cross-key LABEL drift found (distinct from the glossary-vs-file staleness above): within a single language the two calculators disagree on the SG term — mtc_sgrock uses a weight-flavored label while rc_sg uses a relative-density-flavored one — in pt (Gravidade específica vs Densidade relativa), uk (Питома вага vs Відносна густина), ar (الكثافة النوعية vs الكثافة النسبية), fa (وزن مخصوص نسبی vs چگالی نسبی); sr already noted. Both labels are individually defensible per the cultural-standard rule, but the intra-language inconsistency between the two calculators warrants a future authorized label-consolidation pass. Tips were translated tip-only, labels preserved. [2026-07-21 Task 133 RESOLVED] Authorized label-consolidation pass done: in each affected language mtc_sgrock's divergent weight-flavored label was aligned to rc_sg's relative-density-flavored label (which already matched this entry's dominant-standard translation) — pt→'Densidade relativa da rocha', uk→'Відносна густина каменю', ar→'الكثافة النسبية للصخور', fa→'چگالی نسبی سنگ', sr→'Релативна густина камена'. next_translated.value: Giriş kanalındaki normal derinlik, q<sub>t</sub>'yi iletmek için gerekli savak yükü (H<sub>p</sub>)'ndan az olduğunda, düşü girişinin membasında kısıtlı akış veya göllenme oluşur. Bu genellikle kabul edilebilirdir — göllenme hızı düşürür ve memba erozyonunu önler. next_translated.english: When the normal depth in the inlet channel is less than the weir head (H<sub>p</sub>) required to pass q<sub>t</sub>, restricted flow or ponding occurs upstream of the steep channel inlet. This is generally acceptable — ponding reduces velocity and prevents erosion upstream. To check: use a weir flow calculator to find H<sub>p</sub> for the given q<sub>t</sub> and crest width, and compare it to the inlet channel normal depth. If H<sub>p</sub> exceeds normal depth, ponding will occur.
